6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoverForcesNonInj
7	
8	/-!
9	# The `V`-interval at a MULTI-INDEX atlas: the hypothesis the one-chart no-go was hiding
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverForcesNonInj.lean` proves that coverage at a proper open `V ≠ ⊤` forces
12	the chart map to be non-injective on some test, and `Picard/Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean`
13	refutes both endpoints of the `V`-interval.  **Every one of those statements is about a
14	one-chart atlas** (`ι := PUnit`), and the first file says so twice in its own limits section:
15	
16	> the dichotomy above is for a one-chart atlas … and **not** for `mixedParamChart` at
17	> arbitrary `ι`.  The multi-index case is open and is *not* claimed here.
18	
19	The reason it gives is correct: coverage returns *some* index `i`, not the index `i₀` whose
20	tautological section was tested, and if `i ≠ i₀` the two chart values live on different sources,
21	so no non-injectivity of a single map follows.
22	
23	But the seam consumes `mixedParamChart` at arbitrary `ι`
24	(`pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre`, `Pic0ChartRestrictedFibre.lean:259`).  So as the
25	tree stands, every "this `V` is dead" fact is about an atlas the assembly does not use, and
26	nothing says whether the interval is constrained at all for the real one.  **This file settles
27	that**, and the answer is that the no-go does *not* propagate — with the obstruction isolated as
28	a named hypothesis rather than left as a caveat.
29	
30	## What the multi-index argument actually proves
31	
32	Run the one-chart proof at a general family.  Coverage at the test `X i₀`, the tautological
33	section of `f i₀`, and a point `t ∉ V i₀` returns `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and
34	`x : ↥W ⟶ ↥(V i)` with
35	
36	```
37	(f i).app (op ↥W) (x ≫ (V i).ι)  =  (f i₀).app (op ↥W) (W.ι)
38	```
39	
40	Two *different* points of the disjoint union of the chart sources therefore carry the same
41	value.  That is `¬ JointlyInjective f`, and it is all the argument gives: joint injectivity is
42	the conjunction of index separation and per-chart injectivity
43	(`jointlyInjective_iff`), and only the second half is what the one-chart theorem concluded.
44	
45	## Why that is a negative answer, proved rather than asserted
46	
47	`IndexSeparated` — distinct indices never share a value — is **free when `ι` is a subsingleton**
48	(`indexSeparated_of_subsingleton`), which is exactly why the one-chart theorem needed no such
49	hypothesis, and it is **refuted by any atlas with two charts sharing a value**
50	(`not_indexSeparated_duplicated`, at a family whose every member is injective).  A glueing
51	atlas has overlapping charts by construction, so index separation is the wrong thing to hope
52	for and the one-chart refutation has no multi-index analogue.
53	
54	The sharp positive form is `not_injective_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_indexSeparated_of_ne_top`:
55	coverage at a proper `V i₀` *plus index separation* refutes injectivity of that chart.  So the
56	escape from the one-chart no-go is precisely index crossing — the "index slack" that
57	`Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` says the atlas is indexed *for*.  That slack is now
58	load-bearing rather than decorative.
59	
60	## The honest limits
61	
62	* **Nothing here discharges an antecedent.**  `PointwiseCoverage` at a proper `V` has no
63	  producer, and neither does its negation; every theorem below is an implication between open
64	  propositions, or a statement about a concrete witness family.  What changes is that the
65	  `V`-interval no-go is now known **not** to close the multi-index route, so a lane may
66	  legitimately aim antecedent 1 at `mixedParamChart` with `ι` genuinely large.
67	* **This is not a claim that the multi-index seam is satisfiable.**  Refuting a refutation is
68	  not an inhabitation.  `(huniv V, hcov V)` remains unmeasured at every `V`, at every `ι`.
69	* **Everything is stated for an arbitrary family of big-site presheaf maps.**  No divisor
70	  scheme, chart index, twist, `rep` or `pic⁰` fact enters any statement or proof, exactly as in
71	  the one-chart file — so nothing here depends on which atlas a producer eventually builds.
72	
73	## Main declarations
74	
75	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JointlyInjective` — the multi-index strengthening of per-test injectivity:
76	  the chart sources inject *jointly* into the Σ-sheaf.
77	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IndexSeparated` — distinct indices never share a value.
78	* `AlgebraicGeometry.jointlyInjective_iff` — joint injectivity **is** index separation plus
79	  per-chart injectivity.  This is the decomposition that shows what the one-chart conclusion was.
80	* `AlgebraicGeometry.not_jointlyInjective_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_ne_top` — **the multi-index
81	  step**: coverage at a proper `V i₀` refutes joint injectivity, at arbitrary `ι`.
82	* `AlgebraicGeometry.not_injective_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_indexSeparated_of_ne_top` — the
83	  one-chart conclusion recovered at arbitrary `ι`, with the missing hypothesis explicit.
84	* `AlgebraicGeometry.indexSeparated_of_subsingleton` — why the one-chart theorem needed none.
85	* `AlgebraicGeometry.not_indexSeparated_duplicated` and
86	  `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_duplicated` — the negative answer: an all-injective family that
87	  is not index separated, so the added hypothesis is not free and the no-go does not propagate.
88	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_crossing_or_not_injective_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_ne_top` — the
89	  dichotomy in the form a coverage lane consumes: the witness crossed to another chart, or the
90	  tested chart is non-injective on the produced open.
91	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_crossing_or_not_injective_mixedParamChart` and
92	  `AlgebraicGeometry.not_pointwiseCoverage_mixedParamChart_of_jointlyInjective` — both
93	  instantiated at `mixedParamChart`, i.e. at the atlas
94	  `pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre` actually takes, so the measurement is about the
95	  real assembly and not about a one-chart stand-in.
96	* `AlgebraicGeometry.jointlyInjective_singleSpecFamily` — the non-vacuity check: joint
97	  injectivity is inhabited, so the refutation above is about the *index* and not about the
98	  Σ-sheaf admitting no injective family at all.
99	* `AlgebraicGeometry.UniformCoverage` and
100	  `AlgebraicGeometry.not_injective_of_uniformCoverage_of_ne_top` — **the useful half**: the
101	  no-go *does* propagate when coverage returns one prescribed index, which is the shape a
102	  chart with full locus supplies.  So the multi-index escape is available exactly to atlases
103	  whose coverage genuinely uses several charts.
104	-/

112

114

122	
123	variable (C) in
124	/-- **Joint injectivity of a chart family**: over every test, the disjoint union of the chart
125	sources injects into the Σ-sheaf.
126	
127	For a one-element family this is per-test injectivity of the single chart map; for a general
128	family it is strictly stronger (`jointlyInjective_iff`, `not_indexSeparated_duplicated`), and it
129	is exactly the statement the multi-index coverage argument refutes. -/
130	def JointlyInjective {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
131	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) : Prop :=
132	  ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) (i j : ι) (x : (yoneda.obj (X i)).obj S)
133	    (y : (yoneda.obj (X j)).obj S),
134	    (f i).app S x = (f j).app S y →
135	      (⟨i, x⟩ : Σ i, (yoneda.obj (X i)).obj S) = ⟨j, y⟩
136	
137	variable (C) in
138	/-- **Index separation**: two charts with different indices never take the same value on a
139	common test.
140	
141	This is the half of joint injectivity that has no one-chart counterpart, and the whole content
142	of the gap between the one-chart no-go and the multi-index case. -/
143	def IndexSeparated {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
144	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) : Prop :=
145	  ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) (i j : ι) (x : (yoneda.obj (X i)).obj S)
146	    (y : (yoneda.obj (X j)).obj S), (f i).app S x = (f j).app S y → i = j
147	
148	/-- **Joint injectivity decomposes**: it is index separation together with per-chart
149	injectivity on every test.
150	
151	Read left to right this says what the multi-index coverage argument's conclusion contains; read
152	right to left it says the one-chart theorem's conclusion (per-chart injectivity) is only *half*
153	of what would be needed to run the refutation at a general `ι`. -/
154	theorem jointlyInjective_iff {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
155	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) :
156	    JointlyInjective C f ↔
157	      IndexSeparated C f ∧ ∀ (i : ι) (S : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ), Function.Injective ((f i).app S) := by
158	  constructor
159	  · intro h
160	    refine ⟨fun S i j x y hxy => ?_, fun i S x y hxy => ?_⟩
161	    · exact congrArg Sigma.fst (h S i j x y hxy)
162	    · exact eq_of_heq (Sigma.mk.injEq .. ▸ h S i i x y hxy).2
163	  · rintro ⟨hsep, hinj⟩ S i j x y hxy
164	    obtain rfl : i = j := hsep S i j x y hxy
165	    exact congrArg (fun z => (⟨i, z⟩ : Σ i, (yoneda.obj (X i)).obj S)) (hinj i S hxy)
166	
167	/-- Joint injectivity implies per-chart injectivity — the direction a lane will reach for. -/
168	theorem injective_of_jointlyInjective {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
169	    {f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (h : JointlyInjective C f)
170	    (i : ι) (S : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) : Function.Injective ((f i).app S) :=
171	  ((jointlyInjective_iff f).mp h).2 i S
172	
173	/-- **Index separation is free for a one-chart atlas** — the reason
174	`not_injective_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_ne_top` needed no such hypothesis, and the reason its
175	proof cannot be read as covering the general case. -/
176	theorem indexSeparated_of_subsingleton {ι : Type u} [Subsingleton ι] {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
177	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) :
178	    IndexSeparated C f :=
179	  fun _ _ _ _ _ _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _
180	
181	/-! ## The multi-index step -/
182	
183	variable (C) in
184	/-- **COVERAGE AT A PROPER `V i₀` REFUTES JOINT INJECTIVITY, AT ARBITRARY `ι`.**
185	
186	The one-chart argument of `not_injective_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_ne_top`, run at a general
187	family: the tautological section of `f i₀`, tested at `X i₀` and read at a point outside
188	`V i₀`, is matched by a coverage witness that factors through `V i` for *some* index `i`.  Those
189	are two different points of the disjoint union of the chart sources with the same value.
190	
191	The conclusion is about the family, not about `f i₀`: that is exactly the loss the one-chart
192	file predicted, made precise.  Nothing beyond the equation is used — no divisor, chart index,
193	twist, `rep`, or `pic⁰` fact. -/
194	theorem not_jointlyInjective_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_ne_top {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
195	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
196	    (i₀ : ι) (hV : V i₀ ≠ ⊤)

63	  paragraph got wrong in its own favour by saying "the only `V` at which the seam can close is
64	  `⊤`": the only thing keeping `⊤` alive is
65	  `not_restrictedChartFibre_top_of_not_injective`, which *consumes* the negative branch.  So
66	  under injectivity the seam is unsatisfiable at **every** `V` — a sharper conclusion than the
67	  dichotomy was claiming (audit `I-1378`).
68	
69	So the fork and the `V`-interval are one question, not two: a lane cannot pick the restriction
70	repair and stay agnostic about the fork.
71	
72	**THE PRECISE LOGICAL FORM, because an earlier version of this paragraph said "*equivalent*" and
73	that is REFUTED** (audit `I-1379`).  Write `N` for the fork's negative branch and `Q` for
74	`chart-restrict`'s conclusion "any working `V` is a proper intermediate open".  What holds is
75	`N → Q`, one direction.  `Q → N` does **not** follow from the three landed facts: `Works ≡ False`
76	satisfies all of them, satisfies `Q` vacuously, and has `N` false.  It needs the extra premise
77	`∃ V, Works V` — and `Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean`'s own §"CORRECTED FRAMING" says that
78	premise has never been measured at any `V`.  So the honest claim is: `Q` is *implied by* the
79	fork's negative branch, and would be equivalent to it given an inhabitant of the seam that
80	nobody has.  Quoting the equivalence without that premise is the "two refutations are not an
81	inhabitation" error this seam has already made once.

83	## The honest limits, stated rather than left for a reviewer
84	
85	* **Nothing here is discharged.**  `PointwiseCoverage` at a proper `V` is a hypothesis with no
86	  producer — it is exactly the open question `chart-restrict` names — and so is its negation.
87	  Every theorem below is an implication between two open propositions.  What is new is that
88	  they are *linked*.
89	* **THE ANTECEDENT IS STRONGER THAN DAT-B COVERAGE, and that is the live vacuity risk here**
90	  (audit `I-1377`).  The hypothesis is coverage by a **single** chart (`ι = PUnit`).  The landed
91	  converse `pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` (`Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.lean`) turns it into
92	  *unrestricted* coverage by that one chart, and thence into the local-surjectivity instance for
93	  a one-chart atlas — which two of this project's own files say should not hold:
94	  `Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean` ("nothing forces one index to work at every point") and
95	  `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` (the atlas "may be indexed by `m`" precisely so different
96	  points can use different charts).  So the hypothesis may well be refutable, in which case
97	  these theorems are true with an antecedent nothing satisfies.  That does **not** damage the
98	  dichotomy — it is a statement about one-chart atlases either way — but a lane must not read
99	  "coverage at a proper `V`" here as DAT-B's coverage.  The multi-index version of the argument
100	  is open; see the next bullet for why it does not go through as written.
101	* **The argument is per-chart, and a multi-index atlas can evade it.**  Coverage at a general
102	  family returns *some* index `i`, not the index whose tautological section was tested; if
103	  `i ≠ i₀` the two chart values live on different sources and no non-injectivity of a single
104	  map follows.  So the dichotomy above is for a one-chart atlas — which is what
105	  `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean` builds and what `IsChartUniv`, `RestrictedChartFibre` and
106	  `restrictedChartFibre_top_iff` are all stated for — and **not** for `mixedParamChart` at
107	  arbitrary `ι`.  The multi-index case is open and is *not* claimed here.
108	* **The conclusion is not free**, and the check for that has to satisfy the theorem's *own*
109	  binders.  `specSecMap_injective` exhibits a map into the Σ-sheaf that is injective on every
110	  test — the one named by the tautological section `⟨𝟙 (Spec k), 1⟩` — **out of a source that
111	  has a proper open** (`bot_ne_top_specObj`).  So `(f, V)` with `V ≠ ⊤` exists at which the
112	  conclusion fails, hence the theorem is a constraint on the pair rather than a fact about the
113	  sheaf, and composing with `not_pointwiseCoverage_of_injective_of_ne_top` refutes coverage
114	  there outright.
115	
116	  **AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS BULLET NAMED THE WRONG WITNESS, and the correction is the
117	  lesson** (audit `I-1377`/`I-1380`).  It cited `restrictChart f ⊥`, injective by
118	  `isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart_bot`.  That is true and **useless here** on two
119	  counts: the source `↥(⊥ : X.Opens)` has a subsingleton open lattice, so it admits no
120	  `V ≠ ⊤` and the theorem cannot be instantiated at it at all; and every map out of
121	  `yoneda.obj ↥⊥` is injective on every test for free, since that presheaf is
122	  subsingleton-valued — so the cited route through the open-immersion criterion was doing no
123	  work either.  A non-vacuity witness must live where the theorem quantifies.
124

129	* `AlgebraicGeometry.not_injective_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_ne_top` — **the step**: coverage for

195	  -- `V ≠ ⊤` gives a point of `X` outside `V`
196	  obtain ⟨t, htV⟩ : ∃ t : X, t ∉ V := by
197	    by_contra h

199	  obtain ⟨W, htW, iu, x, hx⟩ := hcov X (f.app (op X) (𝟙 X)) t

8	/-!
9	# THE ATLAS IS CHART-PARAMETER HETEROGENEOUS — each chart may carry its own `n`
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` establishes that at a chart index legal at parameter
12	`n` the coverage theorem's threshold is forced to equal `n`, and that at `n = g` the resulting
13	hypothesis is false.  Both that file and the review it adjudicates (I-0660) then reason about
14	"the" chart parameter, as though the atlas had one.
15	
16	**It does not, and this file proves it.**  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
17	(`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) takes a family `f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf`
18	indexed by an arbitrary `ι`, with `X : ι → Scheme` and a *per-index* certificate
19	`hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`.  Nothing ties the `X i` together, so nothing ties
20	their chart parameters together either: `mixedParamChart` below builds such a family from a
21	per-index parameter `nn : ι → ℕ`, a per-index representation of `divFunctor C π (nn i)`, and a
22	per-index chart index legal *at that index's own parameter*.
23	
24	## Why this matters, and it changes the shape of the residue
25	
26	The `b = n` calibration is per-chart.  So the question "can coverage use DAT-0a's threshold?"
27	does not have to be answered uniformly: a point whose splitting field has threshold `b_L` can be
28	covered by *the chart whose parameter is `b_L.toNat`*, and a different point by a different
29	chart.  The I-0204 non-uniformity of `m` — no single exponent works for every fibre — is
30	therefore **not** an obstruction to the atlas; it is an argument for an atlas indexed by the
31	threshold, which is what a heterogeneous family is.
32	
33	What this does **not** do, and the honest limit of the observation:
34	
35	* it does not produce the representations.  `mixedParamChart` takes `rep i` as a hypothesis, one
36	  per parameter, and the divisor-representability lane supplies `divFunctor C π g` — a single
37	  parameter.  So the heterogeneous atlas is *admissible* but not yet *inhabited* beyond `n = g`;
38	* it does not discharge `IsChartUniv` at any index (still CERT-Σ-gated, `Pic0ChartPair.lean`);
39	* it says nothing about local surjectivity, which is DAT-B B-6 and is what would actually consume
40	  the freedom.
41	
42	So the correct statement of the residue, refining `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack`'s: **B-5's step 3
43	is a question about which parameters `divFunctor C π n` is representable at, not about
44	reconciling one parameter with one threshold.**  If representability is available only at `n = g`
45	then the slack must go into `Z` (and its legality is open, as recorded there); if it is available
46	at every `n`, coverage can be assembled chart-by-chart against each fibre's own threshold and the
47	`b = n` forcing is harmless.  That is a sharper question than either prior reading, and it is
48	addressed to the divRep lane rather than to this one.
49	
50	## Main declarations
51	
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamChart` — a chart family with a per-index chart parameter.
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart` — its `hf` clause is exactly a
54	  per-index `IsChartUniv`, so heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate.
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamRepresentableBy` — such a family is admissible input to
56	  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`.  **This is the whole point**: the DAT-glue seam never sees a
57	  chart parameter.
58	-/

description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit after each independently useful, verified proof/file/tooling
  change, before a long build or delegated review, and before expanding scope.
  A multi-hour implementation session should normally have several commits; one
  commit is appropriate only when the work is genuinely atomic. The message +
  diff is how progress is read, so use a semantic, math-first subject. Provenance
  trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`

Verdict and findings below. Filed I-1495 (issue), I-1496 (issue), I-1497 (memory).

## Verdict: FAKE PROGRESS on the headline; one sound-but-renamed section

The file is sorry-free and every theorem in it is true. But the central definition is contentless, and the docstring's conclusion is inverted rather than merely overclaimed. The lane measured a shape condition, believed it had measured a hypothesis about the chart maps, and built the module docstring on that belief.

## The decisive fact

`IndexSeparated` (`/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0ChartMultiIndexInterval.lean:143`) mentions `f` but does not constrain it. It is equivalent to `Subsingleton ι` for **every** family, because the project's own `pic0Sigma_obj_subsingleton_of_isEmpty` (`/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean:160`) makes the Σ-sheaf a subsingleton at any empty test, and every `X i` supplies one via its `⊥` open. Compiled, exit 0, at `/tmp/pv/probe2.lean`:

```lean
theorem indexSeparated_iff_subsingleton (f) : IndexSeparated C f ↔ Subsingleton ι
theorem subsingleton_of_jointlyInjective (f) : JointlyInjective C f → Subsingleton ι
```

## Concrete defects

**1. MATH — `:459` `not_indexSeparated_duplicated` is not about the duplicated family.** The same proof refutes `IndexSeparated` for any family with two distinct indices. `injective_duplicated` (`:443`) and the docstring's "at a family whose every member is injective" (`:50`, `:86`) do no work. The two notions do differ, but only because one implies `Subsingleton ι` — the separation is not witnessed by that family, it is automatic. (Answers your question 1: the family *is* genuinely injective and `injective_duplicated` *does* apply to it, so it is not a degenerate-family artifact — but the injectivity is irrelevant to the refutation.)

**2. MATH — `:194` `not_jointlyInjective_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_ne_top` does not need its hypotheses.** At two distinct indices the conclusion is free with `hcov` and `hV` unused (`/tmp/pv/probe3.lean`, `step_free_at_two_indices`). It carries content only at `Subsingleton ι`, i.e. exactly the landed one-chart case. This is the "multi-index step" the docstring headlines at `:80-81`.

**3. MATH — `:341` `not_pointwiseCoverage_mixedParamChart_of_jointlyInjective` is vacuous at the real atlas.** Advertised at `:92-95` as the measurement "about the real assembly and not about a one-chart stand-in". Once the Abel atlas has two indices, `hinj` is unsatisfiable (`/tmp/pv/probe3.lean`, `mixedParam_positive_branch_vacuous`). Answering your question 4 directly: the `mixedParamChart` / `abelSigmaChart` mismatch is **not** a defect — `mixedParamChart` is definitionally `restrictChart (abelSigmaChart …) (V i)` (`/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:94`) and it is the same object `pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre` takes (`/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0ChartRestrictedFibre.lean:259`), so the instantiation is honest and no same-name confusion. The composition is correct and the hypothesis it composes is empty.

**4. MATH/PROSE — `:230` the "sharp positive form" is the landed one-chart theorem.** `not_injective_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_indexSeparated_of_ne_top` follows from `not_injective_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_ne_top` (`Pic0ChartCoverForcesNonInj.lean:190`): `hsep` collapses the coverage to coverage by the single chart `i₀` (`/tmp/pv/probe4.lean`, `sharp_positive_is_onechart`). The claim at `:54-58` that this makes the atlas's "index slack" load-bearing rests on a hypothesis that is just `Subsingleton ι`.

**5. PROSE — the headline `:23-28`, `:45-52` is inverted, not merely overclaimed.** Answering your question 2: the docstring's generalisation from one family to the Abel atlas is *legitimate as a matter of logic* — but for the opposite reason to the one given, and the reason given is false. `IndexSeparated` fails for the Abel atlas too (any two indices), so "the no-go does not propagate via index separation" holds at the real atlas. What is false is `:47-52`'s account of *why*: not "refuted by any atlas with two charts sharing a value", i.e. a fact about overlapping charts, but "never a hypothesis about the charts at all". The file did not discover that a glueing atlas evades the no-go; it discovered that the hypothesis it invented cannot transmit the no-go under any circumstances. `:57-58` "that slack is now load-bearing rather than decorative" is exactly backwards.

**6. PROSE — `:391-393` steps past what is proved.** "A coverage lane producing such a chart is therefore also producing the `⊤`-end refutation for the real atlas." `not_injective_of_uniformCoverage_of_ne_top` requires `hV : V i₀ ≠ ⊤`; a chart "whose locus is the whole test" is the `V i₀ = ⊤` case, which the theorem excludes. Also the tree's actual uniform producer, `exists_uniform_admissibleCoverageChart_eq_univ` (`/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageThreshold.lean`), yields `chartLocus C m Z lam.1 = Set.univ` — a set on a *test*, not an open of the chart *source* `(D i).left`; `Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.lean:139-142` says those are not interchangeable and owes the `chartLocusOpens` bridge. Same for `:100-103` and `:366`.

## What survived the attack

- **`UniformCoverage` is not unsatisfiable and not equivalent to `PointwiseCoverage`** (question 3). It is definitionally the one-chart `PointwiseCoverage` of the single map `f i₀`, both directions compiled (`/tmp/pv/probe3.lean`, `uniformCoverage_iff_pointwise_single`); the arbitrary-ι direction genuinely fails, and `pointwiseCoverage_of_uniformCoverage` (`:374`) is the correct one-way implication. So `:395` and `:418` are sound — but they are the landed one-chart theorem with the hypothesis renamed (I re-derived `:395` from it in three lines), not new mathematics, and "the useful half of the multi-index measurement" (`:390`, `:100`) oversells that.
- **`JointlyInjective` genuinely is stronger than per-chart injectivity** and the Σ-equality does not collapse: `jointlyInjective_iff` (`:154`) is a correct decomposition, both directions. It is stronger only by carrying `Subsingleton ι`, which is why it is unsatisfiable at the real multi-index atlas.
- **`jointlyInjective_singleSpecFamily` (`:480`) is a real non-vacuity witness** for `JointlyInjective` — but only at `PUnit`, so it does not rescue defect 3. Its docstring claim ("the refutation is about the *index*, not about the Σ-sheaf admitting no injective family") is true and, read with defect 1, is closer to the actual finding than the module docstring is.
- **No duplication found** (question 5). Nothing here re-proves anything in `Pic0ChartCoverForcesNonInj.lean` or `Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean` by name or by statement; `:395` is derivable from the former but is not a transcription of it. `JointlyInjective`, `IndexSeparated` and `UniformCoverage` are new names nowhere else in the tree.
- **Every theorem compiles and no proof is mathematically wrong.** The defects are all in what the statements are claimed to mean.

## Convergence read

Five commits, all one file, growing monotonically — no helper churn, no sorry-stall, no repeated PARTIAL. Mechanically this looks like a clean lane. The problem is direction, not throughput: the lane's own honest-limits section (`:60-71`) audits the right things (no antecedent discharged, refuting a refutation is not inhabitation, no divisor content) and misses the one that matters, which is whether its new hypothesis says anything about the maps it quantifies over. The `UniformCoverage` section, added last, is the part with genuine (if modest) value and is the piece to keep.
